mainTopic: Mixtures of forbidden and permitted food: the order of falling in, the principle of רואין, and when the same kind forbids with any amount (טבל and יין נסך).
overview: The גמרא brings a disagreement about a mixture of permitted wine, water, and forbidden wine. חזקיה says it depends on which wine fell in last, and רבי יוחנן says the mixture is permitted either way. רבי ירמיה suggests this matches the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about two leavens in a dough. The גמרא rejects that suggestion using אביי's explanation of רבי אליעזר. Instead, it says the two disagree about רואין, whether we treat the permitted wine as if it isn't there. It then proves that רבי יוחנן finally ruled that we do. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule: the same kind forbids with any amount, and a different kind forbids only by giving taste. רב and שמואל apply this rule to all Torah prohibitions, while רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש apply the strict same-kind rule only to טבל and יין נסך, and each side has a supporting ברייתא. Finally the גמרא explains why טבל is strict: just as one grain of תרומה permits a whole heap, a tiny bit of טבל forbids a mixture of its own kind.

steps.title: חזקיה: it depends on which wine came last
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה rules that if the forbidden wine made the mixture bigger (it fell in last), the mixture is forbidden. If the permitted wine made it bigger (it fell in last), the mixture is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: If they made it bigger with the forbidden wine, it is forbidden. If they made it bigger with the permitted wine, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives his ruling about a mixture of wine and water, based on which wine was added last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters to חזקיה. If the forbidden wine comes last, it touches permitted wine of its own kind, and the water cannot cancel it out, so everything is forbidden. If the forbidden wine was already cancelled out in the water before the permitted wine fell in, the permitted wine stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it bigger, meaning they added the last part to the mixture
With the forbidden thing (here, יין נסך)
With the permitted thing (here, kosher wine)

steps.whatToRemember: For חזקיה, the order of falling in decides everything: forbidden wine last means forbidden, permitted wine last means permitted.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
If they increased it with the forbidden wine, it is forbidden;
phrases.notes: "Increased it" means the forbidden wine was the last thing to fall into the mixture.

phrases.english: if they increased it with the permitted wine, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first opinion about a mixture of wine and water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mixture's status depends on which wine fell in last: forbidden wine last means forbidden, permitted wine last means permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: permitted even if the forbidden wine came last
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with חזקיה. He says the mixture is permitted even when the forbidden wine was the last to fall in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even if they made it bigger with the forbidden wine, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with חזקיה and says the mixture is permitted in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "even" (אפילו) shows that רבי יוחנן is targeting חזקיה's first case. For רבי יוחנן the order does not matter, and the mixture is permitted either way. Step 7 explains why: he treats the permitted wine as if it isn't there, so the water alone cancels the forbidden wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, which marks the case where he goes further than חזקיה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even if they increased it with the forbidden wine, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with חזקיה's first case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mixture is permitted even when the forbidden wine fell in last.

steps.title: Is this the same argument as רבי אליעזר and the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether חזקיה and רבי יוחנן are simply repeating an older dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Shall we say that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן are arguing about the same thing that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה suggests that this argument may be the same as an older one from the תנאים. This sets up the source the גמרא is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לימא" (shall we say) offers a suggestion that the גמרא often tests and sometimes rejects. If the link holds, then each of these אמוראים would be siding with a different תנא. The older dispute is about two things together causing a result.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say, which introduces a suggestion that may be tested or rejected
In the dispute of
They are arguing
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
Shall we say that Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan
disagree about the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא חִזְקִיָּה וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to connect the dispute in steps 1–2 to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן matches the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה about two leavens that together made dough rise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה in ערלה. Leaven of חולין and leaven of תרומה fell into dough. Neither one alone was strong enough to make the dough rise, but together they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Leaven of חולין and leaven of תרומה fell into a dough. This one alone was not enough to make it rise, and that one alone was not enough to make it rise, but they joined together and made it rise...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the older dispute it just mentioned. This sets up the comparison, and the next step gives the two opinions in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has a forbidden-type ingredient (תרומה, which a non-כהן may not eat) and a permitted ingredient (חולין). Each is too weak on its own, but together they cause a result. The question is whether the תרומה is counted as a cause. That is similar to asking whether forbidden wine added to a mixture matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough leaven used to make dough rise
Ordinary, non-holy food
The holy portion given to a כהן, forbidden to others
To make the dough rise
And they joined together

steps.confusionAlert: This step only sets out the case. The dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: As we learned: Non-sacred leaven and teruma leaven
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in ערלה 2:11.

phrases.english: that fell into the dough,
and there is not enough in this one to cause leavening,
nor enough in that one to cause leavening,
and they combined and caused it to leaven,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that contains the dispute mentioned in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן follow the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 2:11, about חולין leaven and תרומה leaven that combined to make dough rise.

steps.title: The two opinions in the leaven משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with the dispute: רבי אליעזר says the last leaven to fall in decides. The חכמים say the dough is forbidden only if the forbidden leaven alone could have made it rise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: I go by the last one that fell in. The חכמים say: whether the forbidden leaven fell in first or last, the dough is not forbidden unless the forbidden leaven alone has enough strength to make it rise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in the last step. These are the two opinions that רבי ירמיה wanted to compare to חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's "last one decides" sounds just like חזקיה, who said it depends on which wine fell in last. The חכמים ignore the order and only ask whether the forbidden part is strong enough alone, which sounds like רבי יוחנן. So the suggestion from step 3 looks reasonable at first.

keyTerms.meaning: I go after the last one: the last ingredient to fall in decides the law
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה
Enough to make the dough rise (become leavened)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
I go after the last one,
phrases.notes: He means whichever leaven fell into the dough last decides whether it's forbidden.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנָּפַל אִיסּוּר בַּתְּחִלָּה וּבֵין בַּסּוֹף —
phrases.english: whether the forbidden one fell in first or last —
it is not forbidden
unless there is enough in it [by itself] to make [the dough] rise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַר אַחֲרוֹן אֲנִי בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quotation begun in step 4, giving the two opinions to compare.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that חזקיה = רבי אליעזר and רבי יוחנן = חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ערלה about חולין and תרומה leaven falling into dough

steps.title: אביי's reading leaves חזקיה matching no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. אביי said רבי אליעזר permits the dough only if the forbidden leaven was removed first. If so, חזקיה's ruling fits neither רבי אליעזר nor the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? Didn't אביי say: רבי אליעזר only taught that the dough is permitted when the forbidden leaven was removed first. If it was not removed first, the dough is forbidden. So whose opinion does חזקיה follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the idea that the two arguments are the same. It uses אביי's explanation of רבי אליעזר to show that חזקיה can't fit either side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, רבי אליעזר forbids the dough even when the permitted leaven fell in last, unless the forbidden leaven was taken out first. In חזקיה's wine case nothing was taken out, so רבי אליעזר would forbid it either way. But חזקיה permits it when the permitted wine fell in last. The חכמים would permit it either way, but חזקיה forbids it when the forbidden wine fell in last. So חזקיה matches no one.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you think so?! An opening that rejects the idea just raised
He first removed (the forbidden item before the permitted one fell in)
Like whom? Which opinion does this follow?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read אביי as arguing with רבי אליעזר. He is explaining him: "last one decides" only helps if the forbidden leaven was already taken out.

phrases.english: And can you think so?!
But didn't Abaye say:
They only taught [this]
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי אליעזר's ruling that the dough is permitted when the permitted leaven fell in last.

phrases.english: where he first removed the forbidden [leaven],

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא קָדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if he did not first remove the forbidden [leaven], it is forbidden.
Chizkiyah, who said [his ruling], is like whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison suggested by the משנה in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חזקיה follows רבי אליעזר (and רבי יוחנן follows the חכמים)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Per אביי, רבי אליעזר forbids whenever the forbidden item was not removed first, and the חכמים always permit when the forbidden item is too weak by itself. חזקיה's order-based ruling fits neither.

steps.title: They really argue about רואין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about רואין, whether we treat the permitted wine of the same kind as if it isn't there. חזקיה does not hold of it, and רבי יוחנן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about רואין. חזקיה does not hold of רואין, and רבי יוחנן does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the comparison to the משנה and offers a different reason for the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רואין means we look at the permitted wine, which is the same kind as the forbidden wine, as if it were not there. Then only the water is left to cancel the forbidden wine. רבי יוחנן holds this, so the water cancels the forbidden wine and the mixture is always permitted. חזקיה does not hold this, so the result depends on other factors like which wine fell in last.

keyTerms.meaning: We view: we treat the permitted item of the same kind as if it weren't there, so the different-kind item can cancel the forbidden one
They argue (about this point)
He holds of it / he does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא no longer says חזקיה and רבי יוחנן repeat רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. Their argument is about רואין.

phrases.english: Rather, here they argue about "we view":
phrases.notes: "We view" means we look at the permitted wine as if it isn't there, so the water alone can cancel the forbidden wine.

phrases.english: Chizkiyah does not hold of "we view,"
Rabbi Yochanan does hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of step 6 by giving a new basis for the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן repeat the dispute of רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about the principle of רואין: רבי יוחנן holds of it and חזקיה does not.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really hold of רואין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן about two diluted cups, one חולין and one תרומה, mixed together, and רבי יוחנן did not answer. So it seems he had no firm view on רואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יוחנן hold of רואין? Didn't רבי אסי ask רבי יוחנן: two cups, one of חולין and one of תרומה, and he diluted them with water and mixed them together. What is the law? And he did not answer him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 7. It brings a case where רבי יוחנן was unsure about רואין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-cups case, the water cancels the תרומה wine only if we ignore the חולין wine, which is exactly רואין. If רבי יוחנן clearly held of רואין, he would have answered "permitted." His silence suggests he was not sure about רואין, which would weaken step 7. Step 9 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question of law)
Cups (of wine)
He diluted them with water
Resolved (a question)

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רוֹאִין?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yochanan hold of "we view"?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yochanan:
Two cups, one of ordinary wine
and one of terumah,
and he diluted them and mixed them with each other — what is [the law]?
And he did not resolve it for him!
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads his silence as a sign he wasn't sure about "we view." Step 9 answers this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רוֹאִין? וְהָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 by questioning רבי יוחנן's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds of רואין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן was unsure in רבי אסי's two-cups case, which depends on רואין. So he can't be said to clearly hold of רואין.

steps.title: At first he didn't answer, but later he did
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's silence was only at first. Later he gave a clear answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he did not answer him. In the end he did answer him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8. רבי יוחנן's silence was only at first, and later he gave a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that רבי יוחנן had no firm view on רואין, because he did not answer רבי אסי. The answer is that he only held back at the start. Later he ruled that we do ignore the permitted wine, so step 7's explanation of רבי יוחנן still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: at first, originally
he answered him, he settled the question for him
in the end, later on

phrases.english: At first he did not answer him,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, and 'him' is רבי אסי, who asked about the two cups in step 8.

phrases.english: in the end he answered him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא פְּשַׁט לֵיהּ, לְבַסּוֹף פְּשַׁט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the timing: silence at first, a ruling later.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's silence means he had no firm view on רואין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He later ruled that we hold of רואין, so the dispute with חזקיה still works.

steps.title: A report proves רבי יוחנן ruled that we ignore the permitted wine
steps.stepSummary: A report in the name of רבי יוחנן says: with two diluted cups, one חולין and one תרומה, mixed together, we treat the permitted wine as if it isn't there, and the water cancels the תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some say it was רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: two cups, one of חולין and one of תרומה, which were diluted with water and mixed together. We look at the permitted wine as if it isn't there, and the water is more than the rest and cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a recorded ruling of רבי יוחנן to back up the claim that he did finally answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same two-cup case רבי אסי asked about. Here רבי יוחנן clearly rules רוֹאִין: ignore the חולין wine and compare the תרומה wine against the water alone. Since there is more water than תרומה wine, the תרומה is cancelled and the mix is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated; a report that supports what was just said
he diluted them with water
are more than it
cancel it, so the forbidden part loses its status

steps.confusionAlert: Don't compare the תרומה wine against all the liquid, wine and water together. The permitted wine is set aside as if it isn't there, and only the water counts against the תרומה.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Two cups of wine,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאֶחָד שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred wine and one of terumah,
and he diluted them and mixed them together,
we view the permitted wine as if it is not there,
and as for the rest, the water is more than it
phrases.notes: 'The rest' is the תרומה wine that is left once we set aside the permitted wine.

phrases.english: and cancels it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9 with a recorded ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן finally ruled that we hold of רואין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling of רבי יוחנן reported by רבי אמי, or by רבי אסי, about the two diluted cups.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds רוֹאִין: permitted wine of the same kind is ignored, and only the water is weighed against the forbidden wine. This keeps step 7's explanation of the dispute with חזקיה in place.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: same kind with any amount, different kind with taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. The same kind forbids with any amount, and a different kind forbids only if it gives taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: a kind mixed with its own kind is forbidden with any amount. Mixed with a different kind, it is forbidden only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It quotes it so it can discuss it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a forbidden food mixes with permitted food of the same kind, even a tiny bit forbids the whole mixture. If it mixes with a different kind, the mixture is forbidden only if you can taste the forbidden food in it.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the rule; a general principle
a kind mixed with its own kind
with any amount, even a tiny bit
only when it gives taste

phrases.english: This is the rule:
a kind with its own kind is forbidden with any amount,
with a different kind, only when it gives taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section: the גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same kind forbids with any amount. A different kind forbids only when it gives taste.

steps.title: רב and שמואל apply this rule to all Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both say the same-kind and different-kind rule applies to every forbidden food in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: all the prohibitions in the Torah, with their own kind, are forbidden with any amount. With a different kind, only when they give taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from רב and שמואל that takes the משנה's rule and widens it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is speaking about יין נסך. רב and שמואל say the same rule is true for every Torah prohibition. This sets up the next question about why the משנה says 'this is the rule.'

keyTerms.meaning: both of them
the prohibitions in the Torah, foods the Torah forbids

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a rule about יין נסך into a general rule for mixtures of any forbidden food.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
all the prohibitions in the Torah,
with their own kind, are forbidden with any amount,
with a different kind, only when they give taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the משנה's rule from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every Torah prohibition forbids with any amount in its own kind, and only by taste in a different kind.

steps.title: What does 'this is the rule' come to add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'this is the rule' add, according to רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule.' What does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה used the words 'this is the rule.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'rule' usually means the משנה is reaching past its own case. The גמרא wants to know which extra cases the rule covers.

keyTerms.meaning: to include what? What does this come to add?

phrases.english: This is the rule: what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה, in light of רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra cases the משנה's word 'rule' is meant to include.

steps.title: It includes all Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: 'This is the rule' comes to include all the prohibitions in the Torah, not just יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include all the prohibitions in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'rule' extends the משנה's law to every Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רב and שמואל's statement. The משנה itself, by saying 'this is the rule,' teaches that the same-kind and different-kind law is not only for יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: to include, to bring in more cases

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב and שמואל, 'this is the rule' in the משנה widens the law to all Torah prohibitions. In the same kind, any amount forbids. In a different kind, only taste forbids.

phrases.english: To include all the prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'rule' includes every Torah prohibition, not only יין נסך.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: most prohibitions need taste, except two
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say every Torah prohibition, same kind or different kind, forbids a mixture only by נותן טעם. The exceptions are טבל and יין נסך, which forbid with any amount in their own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: for all the prohibitions in the Torah, whether mixed with their own kind or a different kind, the mixture is forbidden only when the forbidden food gives taste. The exception is טבל and יין נסך. With their own kind they forbid with any amount, and with a different kind only when they give taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with רב and שמואל about how wide the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל said the 'same kind forbids with any amount' rule covers every prohibition. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say the normal rule is נותן טעם across the board. Only two special items, טבל and יין נסך, get the strict 'any amount' rule when mixed with their own kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them (said the same thing)
With its own kind, mixed with the same type of food
Gives taste: forbidden only if the forbidden food can be tasted in the mixture
With any amount, even the tiniest bit
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken
Wine poured or used for עבודה זרה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. Both agree that a different kind needs taste. They only argue about the same kind: רב and שמואל say any amount for every prohibition, while רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say any amount only for טבל and יין נסך.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish, who both say:
All the prohibitions in the Torah,
whether with their own kind or not with their own kind,
forbid only when they give taste,
except for טבל and יין נסך,
which with their own kind forbid with any amount,
and not with their own kind, only when they give taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing view to רב and שמואל (step 12) about how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Torah prohibitions follow נותן טעם, in the same kind and in a different kind, except טבל and יין נסך, which forbid with any amount in their own kind.

steps.title: For רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, 'this is the rule' adds טבל
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, the משנה's phrase 'this is the rule' comes to include טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the words 'this is the rule' come to include טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same question as step 13, what 'this is the rule' adds, but now according to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב and שמואל, the phrase widened the rule to every prohibition. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש don't widen it that far. For them it adds just one more item, טבל, which the משנה never mentioned by name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is the rule': the משנה's general summary wording
To include, to bring in something extra

phrases.english: And 'this is the rule'
comes to include טבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש by explaining the משנה's wording on their terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'this is the rule' add, according to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש (the question from step 13).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They come to include טבל in the strict 'any amount' rule for the same kind.

steps.title: Each side has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא matches רב and שמואל and another ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught like רב and שמואל, and a ברייתא is taught like רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that both opinions have a ברייתא behind them, and it is about to quote each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view is pushed aside. Each one has older support from a ברייתא. The next two steps spell out the exact wording of each.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him, matching his view

phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rav and Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: and it is taught in line with Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both opinions are laid out, it announces that each has support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions are backed by a ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא that matches רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that for all Torah prohibitions, the same kind forbids with any amount and a different kind forbids only by taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught like רב and שמואל: all the prohibitions in the Torah, with their own kind, forbid with any amount; not with their own kind, only when they give taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that supports רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'all the prohibitions in the Torah' and lists no exceptions. That is exactly what רב and שמואל said: the strict same-kind rule covers everything, not just יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibitions in the Torah, foods the Torah forbids

phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rav and Shmuel:
All the prohibitions in the Torah,
with their own kind, forbid with any amount;
not with their own kind, only when they give taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the announcement in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רב and שמואל that the same-kind rule applies to every Torah prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that all Torah prohibitions forbid with any amount in their own kind, with no exceptions listed.

steps.title: The ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that all Torah prohibitions forbid only by taste, except טבל and יין נסך, which forbid with any amount in their own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught like רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: all the prohibitions in the Torah, whether with their own kind or not, forbid only when they give taste. The exception is טבל and יין נסך: with their own kind, any amount; not with their own kind, only when they give taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, which matches the view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא makes נותן טעם the normal rule for everything. It singles out only טבל and יין נסך for the strict same-kind rule. So the disagreement between the אמוראים mirrors a disagreement already found between two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... or... (covering both cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Different kind: everyone agrees it forbids only by taste. Same kind: רב and שמואל say any amount for every prohibition, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say any amount only for טבל and יין נסך. Each side has a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish:
All the prohibitions in the Torah,
whether with their own kind or not with their own kind,
forbid only when they give taste,
except for טבל and יין נסך,
which with their own kind forbid with any amount;
not with their own kind, only when they give taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second half of the announcement in step 17, parallel to step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that only טבל and יין נסך forbid with any amount in their own kind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that all prohibitions follow נותן טעם, except טבל and יין נסך.

steps.title: Why is טבל an exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why יין נסך is strict, but asks what reason makes טבל forbid with any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for יין נסך, because עבודה זרה is so severe. But טבל, what is the reason it is so strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the exceptions that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש made in Step 15. It accepts one exception and asks for the reason behind the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said every Torah prohibition needs נותן טעם, except טבל and יין נסך. For יין נסך the strictness is easy to explain, because anything connected to עבודה זרה is treated very severely. טבל has no such obvious reason, so the גמרא asks why it gets the same strict treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' question)
Severity, strictness
Idol worship
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, wine used for a libation,
is strict because of the severity of idol worship,
but untithed produce, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא יֵין נֶסֶךְ, מִשּׁוּם חוּמְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֶלָּא טֶבֶל מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the טבל exception in the ברייתא and the ruling of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason טבל forbids its own kind with any amount, when יין נסך has a clear reason (the severity of עבודה זרה) and טבל seems to have none.

steps.title: Forbidding works the same way as permitting
steps.stepSummary: Because a tiny amount of תרומה permits a whole heap, a tiny amount of טבל forbids a whole mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: The way it becomes permitted is the way it forbids. As שמואל said: one grain of wheat exempts the whole heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a symmetry: טבל forbids in the same way it gets fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that even one grain separated as תרומה is enough to make a whole heap permitted. Since such a tiny amount can permit the whole heap, it fits that a tiny amount of טבל can forbid a whole mixture of its own kind. That is what makes טבל special, even though it has nothing to do with עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: As its permitting, so is its forbidding
One grain of wheat
Exempts, releases from the obligation
A heap or pile of grain
The portion of produce given to the כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the strictness of טבל comes from how טבל itself works, not from how severe the sin is.

phrases.english: As is its permitting, so is its forbidding,
as שמואל said:
One grain of wheat exempts the whole heap.
phrases.notes: He means one grain given as תרומה. That is enough to make the whole heap permitted to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טבל forbids with any amount because it is also fixed by any amount: one grain of תרומה permits the whole heap, so it makes sense that a tiny bit of טבל forbids a whole mixture.

steps.title: A ברייתא: טבל is strict only with its own kind
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the idea that טבל forbids with any amount, but only when it is mixed with its own kind. With a different kind it needs נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught so: In what case did they say טבל forbids with any amount? In its own kind. With a different kind, only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the special rule for טבל and to show its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that טבל really does forbid with any amount, which matches the exception in Step 19. It also adds a limit: the strict rule applies only when טבל is mixed with the same kind of food. With a different kind, טבל goes back to the normal rule of נותן טעם.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
In what case did they say? (introduces a limit on a rule)
With any amount at all
With its own kind
With a different kind

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, טבל forbids its own kind with any amount, because a tiny amount of תרומה permits a whole heap. Mixed with a different kind, טבל forbids only by נותן טעם.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think טבל always forbids with any amount. The strict rule is only for a mixture of the same kind.

phrases.english: And it is also taught so:
In what case did they say
that untithed produce forbids with any amount?
With its own kind;
with a different kind, only when it gives taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings ברייתא support for the טבל rule explained in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That טבל forbids with any amount in its own kind, and only by taste in a different kind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'בַּמֶּה אָמְרוּ טֶבֶל אוֹסֵר בְּכׇל שֶׁהוּא? בְּמִינוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.'
